llm.reply:
The KRAS gene encodes a protein that functions within the small GTPase superfamily [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. This protein's primary molecular activity involves acting as a molecular switch to activate downstream cellular pathways [26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways"].

## GTPase Function
The KRAS product is a GTPase [4]. It acts as a member of the small GTPase superfamily [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. The activity of this protein is driven by a guanosine exchange factor [29: "guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1 that drives KRAS"]. 

## Downstream Signaling
When functioning as a molecular switch, the KRAS protein activates signaling pathways that control cellular proliferation and survival [26: "stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival"]. Genetic alterations can lead to the constant activation of this protein [26: "mutations result in constitutive activation of the KRAS protein"]. This persistent signaling ultimately contributes to cancer development [26: "leading to tumorigenesis"].

The encoded protein functions as a member of the GTPase class [11: "member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. It operates as an active signaling switch [26: "molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways"]. The gene symbol is KRAS [1].
